overview.title: Where the Catch Comes In
overview.p1: Essaouira’s port is still a working fishing harbour. Blue wooden boats crowd the quays, nets dry in the wind, and seagulls dive for scraps. This is not a staged attraction — the catch lands here every morning and the grills fire up soon after.
overview.p2: Climb the Skala platform above the harbour for cannons, stone walls and a full view of the fleet. Then drop back to the stalls: point to a fish, agree the price, and watch it hit the plancha.
overview.p3: Combine the port with Place Moulay Hassan and a short medina loop in the same half-day. Bring a light jacket — the alizé rarely rests.

food.title: Eat at the Quay
food.p1: The port is the best place in Essaouira to eat fish the same day it was landed.
food.li1: Grilled sardines or sea bream at a harbour stall
food.li2: Fish soup before the main grill
food.li3: Mint tea on Place Moulay Hassan after lunch
food.li4: A rooftop riad dinner if you want a longer meal
food.li5: Orange juice near the medina gate
food.p2: Stalls are informal and shared. For a quieter table, walk two minutes into the medina.

q1.question: Is the port free?
q1.answer: Yes. The harbour and Skala exterior are free; you pay only for food or boat trips.

q2.question: How do I order fish?
q2.answer: Choose the fish, confirm the price and cooking style before it is grilled. Cash is standard.

q3.question: Can I visit the islands from here?
q3.answer: Landing is restricted; ask licensed operators about legal boat circuits only.

q4.question: Do I need a guide at Skala du Port?
q4.answer: Optional for a simple visit; useful for history and local context.

q5.question: Is Skala du Port suitable for families?
q5.answer: Yes with normal supervision near drops, wind or busy lanes.
